original_question: Determine how adding nonlocal information gathering to conflict-memory dynamics changes space-use outcomes by comparing the qualitative properties of non-constant steady states in the nonlocal conflict-generation model against those in the local conflict-zone memory model.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2.2, Open Problem 19: compare the qualitative features of spatially non-constant steady states for problem (2.16) with those for problem (2.13), i.e. ask how nonlocal information gathering changes space-use outcomes in the conflict-memory setting. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft correctly captures the paper’s intended comparison: it is about space-use outcomes interpreted through qualitative properties of spatially non-constant steady states, and it identifies the relevant modification as adding nonlocal information gathering to a conflict-memory model. That is exactly the conceptual content of Open Problem 19, which compares problem (2.16) against problem (2.13). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not identify the paper’s official target by name and number: the nearest formulation is Open Problem 19 in Section 2.2.2, explicitly comparing problems (2.16) and (2.13). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the paper’s steady-state setup: the comparison is posed in the periodic bounded-domain setting with a top-hat detection function, inherited from Open Problem 18 for (2.16) and Open Problem 10 for (2.13). ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It does not define the variables: u_i(x,t) are interacting population densities and k_i(x,t) are spatial memories of conflict zones. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It does not define the perception operator used throughout the models, namely a^{g,R}(x,t)=∫_Ω a(y,t)g(x-y)dy, nor the top-hat detection kernel and perceptual radius R. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It does not make explicit where the nonlocality changes: both models already use nonlocal perception in the advection term through k_i^{g,R}; the difference between (2.16) and (2.13) is specifically that conflict generation becomes nonlocal, replacing u_i∑_jρ_iju_j by u_i^{g,R}∑_jρ_iju_j. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It omits the nearby parameter information needed for a stand-alone formulation: d_i>0, γ_i≥0, ρ_ij as encounter rates, μ≥0 for memory decay, β≥0 for conflict-zone decay, and in model (2.16) the same perceptual kernel and radius are assumed for each population. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

It does not state that the question is only about spatially non-constant steady states, usually conditional on existence; existence and qualitative properties for (2.16) are posed separately in Open Problem 18, while the analogous steady-state question for (2.13) appears in Open Problem 10. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))

Ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restrictions, and nilpotency conditions are not part of this PDE problem, so those categories are not applicable here. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
refined_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions, let g be the top-hat detection kernel with perceptual radius R, and for any scalar field f define f^{g,R}(x,t)=∫_Ω f(y,t)g(x-y)dy. For n interacting populations u_i(x,t) with conflict-memory maps k_i(x,t), compare the spatially non-constant steady states of the local conflict-zone memory model ∂_t u_i=d_iΔu_i+γ_i∇·(u_i∇k_i^{g,R}), ∂_t k_i=u_i∑_{j=1}^nρ_iju_j−(μ+βu_i)k_i, and the nonlocal conflict-generation model ∂_t u_i=d_iΔu_i+γ_i∇·(u_i∇k_i^{g,R}), ∂_t k_i=u_i^{g,R}∑_{j=1}^nρ_iju_j−(μ+βu_i)k_i, where d_i>0, γ_i≥0, ρ_ij≥0, μ≥0, β≥0, and the same kernel/radius are used for each population. Assuming such spatially non-constant steady states exist in this periodic top-hat setting, how do their qualitative features differ between the two models, and hence how does nonlocal conflict generation alter the predicted space-use outcomes relative to model (2.13)? ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Open Problem 19. In the surrounding discussion, the paper first introduces model (2.13), where conflict zones are remembered but conflicts are generated locally, and then proposes model (2.16) as the extension in which agents may experience conflict at a distance and remember those stand-offs as well. Open Problem 18 asks about existence and qualitative properties of spatially non-constant steady states for (2.16), while Open Problem 10 provides the analogous steady-state context for (2.13). Because the draft asks specifically how the added nonlocal information changes space-use outcomes through a comparison of non-constant steady states, Open Problem 19 is the nearest and sharpest official formulation; broader questions about all dynamics, other boundary conditions, or other memory models would go beyond the paper’s intent. ([math.ualberta.ca](https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~hwang/WangSalmaniwReview.pdf))
